newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-TOP PLAYERS OFFERED CHANCE TO BROADEN HORIZONS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TOP PLAYERS OFFERED CHANCE TO BROADEN HORIZONS.

text.p: Golf's leading names could be playing for new world titles in strokeplay, matchplay and team play from 1999 following a meeting of the American, European and other tours.
Nearly two years after Greg Norman announced a breakaway World Tour which never materialised the sport's governing bodies have formed the PGA Tours International Federation.

Tim Finchem, commissioner of the US Tour, said on Sunday: "We feel we need a federation to help promote the game internationally and we also see a need to provide more opportunities, including at least three world championship events, for the top-ranked players in the world to compete internationally.
"They will be organised in such a way so as to enhance existing tour schedules and ensure the major tournaments retain their premier status."
The players taking part will be determined through a world ranking system and Finchem added: "We have proposed certain modifications to the governing structure of the Sony Rankings.
"We will now begin a series of thorough consultations with players, sponsors and other golf organisations concerning these proposals."
